title: Sales enablement 34 Enterprise playbook: positioning, messaging, competitive briefs, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook provides a single, ready-to-use reference for enterprise sales conversations: core positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, recommended pitch-deck flow and talking points, pricing guidance for hosted + Dedicated + Private options, two succinct case studies, and a security FAQ for prospect evaluation. Use this document when preparing enterprise meetings, proposals, and internal enablement.

Audience: Sales reps, solutions engineers, account executives, and customer-facing product managers.

Core product framing

- One-sentence positioning: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted API, reserved Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Primary value props (use in this order):
  1) Predictable economics 4 reduce per-token cost through batching, caching, and model/quantization recommendations while keeping latency SLOs.
  2) Production reliability 4 cross-region routing, model fallback, and SLA-backed Dedicated pools for business-critical applications.
  3) Unified developer experience 4 same API, SDKs, and rollouts across hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
  4) Enterprise controls 4 audit logs, KMS integration, VPC-onboarding, and compliance evidence packages.

Positioning and messaging (elevator 12 expansion)

Elevator pitch (30s): "Redwood Inference helps engineering teams ship LLM-powered features with predictable latency and unit economics 4 whether you want quick time-to-value via our hosted API or enterprise-grade isolation and SLAs via Dedicated and Private deployments. We combine a GPU-optimized serving runtime with operations tooling so product teams stop firefighting inference and focus on product outcomes."

Key messages and proof points (pick 2-3 for each meeting):
- Performance: 50-200ms median token latency on typical instruction workloads (hosted API benchmarks available on request).
- Cost efficiency: customers see 15-40% unit-cost reduction after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, KV cache, quantization).
- Reliability: Dedicated customers get 99.95% uptime with configurable autoscaling and burst capacity.
- Developer experience: SDKs (Python/TS/Go), streaming responses, and function/tool calling for structured outputs.
- Security: VPC/private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, and detailed audit logging.

Proof artifacts to attach to deal folders:
- Host benchmarks: per-model latency/cost matrix for common sequence lengths.
- Architecture diagram for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Redwood Optimize recommendation sample for a representative workload.

Competitive brief (one-page summary)

Competitors covered: MajorCloudAI, FastServeAI, InferenceOps (self-hosted runtimes), and Generic LLM API providers. Use the short brief below when discussing differences.

- MajorCloudAI
  - Positioning: Large cloud vendor with managed model endpoints.
  - Strengths: Deep cloud integration, scale, multi-region networking.
  - Weaknesses / Objections: Higher per-token cost for bursty workloads, limited inference-specific optimizations and model-level rollouts.
  - Redwood counter: We provide inference-first optimizations (KV caching, batching, quantization profiles) and flexible deployment modes that match cloud integration with inference economics.

- FastServeAI
  - Positioning: Startup focusing on low-latency hosted API.
  - Strengths: Aggressive latency claims, developer-friendly API.
  - Weaknesses: Limited enterprise controls (no private/offline options), narrow observability.
  - Redwood counter: Match or beat latency at scale while offering Dedicated and Private deployments plus compliance controls required by enterprise buyers.

- InferenceOps (self-hosted runtime vendors)
  - Positioning: Customers self-host inference runtime for maximum control.
  - Strengths: Full control, potential unit-cost savings at scale.
  - Weaknesses: Heavy ops burden, longer time-to-value, fragmented support.
  - Redwood counter: We offer the same control surface via Dedicated/Private with a managed control plane, onboarding runbooks, and enterprise SLAs to reduce operational risk.

Competitive battlecard: Keep a one-page PDF version attached to opportunity. Include: key objection + 1-2 rebuttals, similar-customer reference, and recommended demo script (see SE demo below).

Pitch deck guidance (recommended slide flow and talking points)

1) Title / Hook - 1 slide: customer logo + 1-line outcome statement we can deliver (e.g., "Cut inference cost by 30% while keeping sub-100ms tail latency").
2) Problem - 1-2 slides: explain operational and economic pain of self-hosting and generic managed endpoints. Use customer metrics (tokens/day, p95 latency, SRE headcount).
3) Redwood value prop - 1 slide: the three-lane approach (Hosted | Dedicated | Private) and quick bullets for economics, reliability, and controls.
4) Architecture - 1 slide: diagram for the recommended deployment (hosted for POC, Dedicated for scale, Private for regulated).
5) Performance & cost evidence - 1-2 slides: benchmark table and Optimize recommendation examples.
6) Security & compliance - 1 slide: controls (VPC, KMS, audit logging, SOC/ISO posture), and what we require for onboarding.
7) Roadmap & integrations - 1 slide: SDKs, partner integrations, and timeline for rollouts.
8) Commercials & next steps - 1 slide: pricing options and recommended pilot scope.

SE demo checklist (pre-demo prep):
- Confirm scope: tokens/day, typical prompt/response length, throughput SLO, data residency needs.
- Prepare 2 benchmarks: median latency and cost per 1M tokens for a representative prompt set.
- Demo flow: quick generation, streaming response, function calling example, and how to configure a canary rollout in console.

Pricing guidance (high-level)

Principles: be transparent, start with anchored POC pricing, expand to committed Dedicated capacity for predictable unit economics, and offer Private with a platform fee plus support.

Suggested pricing tiers (illustrative; finalize with pricing ops):
- Hosted (self-serve): usage-based; example anchor: $0.03 per 1k prompt tokens + $0.12 per 1k completion tokens for model family A. Volume discounts at 10%+ at >100M tokens/month. Embeddings priced separately (e.g., $0.10 per 1k embeddings units).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): baseline monthly commit by GPU equivalent (e.g., a 4xA100 pool). Typical contracts: 6-12 months; discounts on hosted unit rate when committed. Includes SLA (99.95%) and support.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): one-time platform fee + recurring infra support. Pricing depends on packaging (air-gapped vs VPC) and professional services for onboarding.

Commercial negotiation tips:
- Use a 3-month POC hosted engagement with a clearly defined success criteria (p95 latency, cost delta vs prior solution, and feature parity).
- For customers sensitive to cost, propose a dedicated pilot (short-term reserved capacity) with commit and rollback terms.
- Leverage Redwood Optimize findings as a value-add in negotiations - show likely unit-cost delta under realistic traffic patterns.

Case studies (short, sales-ready)

1) FinTech payments platform - "Reduced inference cost and improved latency for fraud scoring"
- Problem: Real-time fraud checks required sub-200ms latency; incumbent approach had high variable cost and inconsistent tail latencies.
- Solution: Deployed Redwood Dedicated with KV caching for common prefixes, worker-level batching, and quantization profile tuned to their scoring model.
- Results: 35% reduction in per-decision inference cost, median latency improved from 260ms to 95ms, and a 3-month ROI achieved by month 4 of Dedicated.
- Contactable reference: available on request (SE to confirm NDA).

2) Healthcare SaaS - "Private deployment for regulated patient messaging"
- Problem: Patient messaging required PHI controls and on-prem deployment in customer's data center.
- Solution: On-prem Private deployment with KMS integration, audit logging, and SSO provisioning. Redwood provided runbooks and two-week on-site support during onboarding.
- Results: Successful SOC2-aligned intake, zero production incidents over first 6 months, and product adoption increased 2x for customer-facing chat features.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers to common enterprise questions)

Q: Where does customer data (prompt + response) reside for Hosted API?
A: By default, hosted requests are processed in the specified cloud region and retained for 30 days for debugging. Customers can opt-out of retention in contract and enable data-only processing in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Q: What encryption standards do you support for data at rest and in transit?
A: TLS1.2+ for transit, AES-256 for data at rest. Private deployments integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM for key control.

Q: How do you support auditability and traceability?
A: We provide structured audit logs (request id, timestamp, user, route, model version) and a retention policy configurable per contract. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM.

Q: Do you support network isolation (VPC/air-gapped)?
A: Yes. We support VPC peering for Private deployments and an on-prem packaging option for air-gapped environments. Professional services required for air-gapped installs.

Q: What certifications or compliance artifacts do you provide?
A: We maintain SOC2 Type II and provide a compliance evidence package for enterprise review. For regulated customers we provide architecture diagrams, data flow docs, and whitebox runbooks as part of an SSO-enabled onboarding.

Q: How do you handle model security (poisoning, prompt injection, privacy)?
A: We recommend a layered approach: (1) prompt filtering and rate limits, (2) model/eval-based guardrails and regression alerts, (3) sandboxed function/tool calling with allowlists, and (4) opt-in model provenance metadata in responses.

Onboarding checklist (recommended scope for an enterprise pilot)

1) Stakeholder alignment: product owner, infra owner, security reviewer (complete).
2) Success criteria: defined p95 latency target, cost baseline, and adoption KPIs (complete).
3) Data & network: region selection, retention agreement, and KMS provisioning (in progress).
4) Pilot configuration: sample prompt set, demo benchmarks, and 4-week pilot runbook (complete).
5) Support plan: assigned SE, onboarding SOW, and escalation contacts (complete).

Assets to attach to opportunity

- One-page competitive battlecard (PDF)
- Performance & cost benchmarking spreadsheet (CSV)
- Pilot SOW template (DOCX)
- Security evidence package (zipped artifacts list)

Next steps for reps and SEs

1) Attach the one-page battlecard and the benchmarking spreadsheet to the opportunity.
2) Schedule a 60-90 minute joint SE + customer workshop to collect sample prompts and define success criteria.
3) Propose a hosted POC or short Dedicated pilot depending on risk tolerance; follow pricing guidance and document the agreed success criteria in the SOW.
